decision: set acceptance to one clean Kubernetes run that kills seven isolation mutants and survives restart
why: the ticket requires production behavior rather than a compile-only proxy

decision: chose one Helm chart with a shared-saas profile, two signed application images, and an external black-box runner
why: this keeps the deployment unit identical to what the test installs

decision: kept one tenant-bound harness process per OIDC principal and gave each Restate service a distinct name
why: a process never has to select trusted tenant from request data

decision: serialized registry publication, Helm install, attacks, mutants, and restart checks inside one cluster lifecycle
why: image digests and cluster state are shared invariants

decision: modeled attacks and mutants as typed evidence rows with redacted tenant references
why: the evidence manifest must prove each boundary without exposing tenant identifiers

decision: used FORCE RLS as defense in depth while retaining explicit tenant predicates
why: the runtime must fail closed both when a predicate is omitted and when session context is absent

decision: restarts application and orchestration workloads before rebuilding DataFusion projections and Brain indexes
why: the proof must cover process replacement and derived-state rebuilds

decision: split deployment readiness at definition activation
why: the harness correctly stayed unready before tenant definitions existed, so Helm could not own both infrastructure readiness and tenant activation
